title: client-segmentation-hitcurve-pricing-sensitivity-jan-2026
content:
SUMMARY:
This is a working workbook + narrative that ties per-client segmentation (usage profile cohorts) to observed prefix/KV cache hit curves and downstream cost/revenue impact under different hosted pricing and Dedicated reserved assumptions. Purpose: give GTM and pricing teams a defensible set of break-even thresholds for offering cache tiers (e.g., per-tenant reserved KV cache buckets, paid add-on) vs recommending automatic cache allocations via Redwood Optimize.

High-level takeaways (working):
- Small fraction of high-throughput clients (Top 5%) drive ~55% of token volume and show early plateauing of per-client incremental hit-rate after ~1200 warm tokens.
- For bursty/short-session cohorts (chatbots with short prompts) prefix cache yields minimal savings unless per-request KV retention is increased beyond 3 requests/session.
- Offering dedicated KV allotments at $X/month becomes positive for clients with >Y requests/day at expected hit-rate >H%. Sensitivity to per-token price (hosted v2 vs reserved) is material.

ASSUMPTIONS AND INPUTS:
- Token unit economics (hosted, baseline): $0.0006 per input token, $0.0018 per output token. (Simplified combined per-token blended cost used in model: $0.0015)
- Dedicated/reserved unit cost (allocated GPUs): effective marginal token cost estimate: $0.0008 blended.
- KV cache storage amortized cost per 100k prefixes/month: $12 (including S3+indexing+ops).
- Average prompt sizes by cohort: small-chat 60 tokens, mid-flow 320 tokens, long-gen 1,800 tokens.
- Hit-curve model per client: we model incremental hit-rate as a logistic curve parametrized by "warm window" (avg prefix reuse window), session length distribution, and prefix entropy. See section "Hit-curve parametrization".

METHODOLOGY (quick):
1) Segment clients into 5 cohorts by 90/50/10 usage percentile: Top(>90th), Upper(75-90), Mid(50-75), Low(10-50), Rare(<10).
2) For each cohort synthesize request traces (N sessions/day, L requests/session, tokens/request) using observed telemetry percentiles (derived from production telemetry sample, anonymized).
3) Simulate KV prefix cache by hashing prompt prefixes into keys; model TTL and per-client allotment, estimate hit-rate curve as function of per-client cache allotment and warm-window parameter.
4) Convert reduced token load to cost savings using both hosted and dedicated unit costs; compute payback on KV allotment cost and potential price differential if charging clients for cache.

SAMPLE COHORT INPUT (text table):
Cohort | %Clients | %TokenVolume | Sessions/day (median) | Avg reqs/session | Avg tokens/req
Top (>90) | 4.8% | 55% | 32 | 6.4 | 520
Upper (75-90) | 11.2% | 20% | 10 | 3.2 | 300
Mid (50-75) | 18.5% | 12% | 4 | 2.1 | 220
Low (10-50) | 32.0% | 9% | 1.2 | 1.6 | 95
Rare (<10) | 33.5% | 4% | 0.2 | 1.1 | 68

HIT-CURVE PARAMETRIZATION (conceptual):
We model per-client prefix hit-rate P(a) as: P(a) = A / (1 + exp(-k*(log10(cache_slots) - m))) where:
- A = asymptotic max hit-rate for the client (depends on prompt entropy)
- k = steepness (how quickly hit-rate increases with more slots)
- m = midpoint in log10(cache_slots) space
Parameters by cohort (defaults used in sims):
Top: A=0.72, k=2.4, m=2.1
Upper: A=0.58, k=2.0, m=1.7
Mid: A=0.42, k=1.6, m=1.3
Low: A=0.28, k=1.2, m=0.9
Rare: A=0.15, k=0.8, m=0.6

SCENARIO EXAMPLES (per-client effective monthly ROI):
Scenario A (conservative): hosted token cost $0.0015, KV allotment buckets sold as add-on at $30/month for 10k slots.
- Top cohort typical hit-rate at 10k slots -> P=0.56 -> token reduction ~ (P * avg output tokens) -> monthly token volume reduction = ~45M tokens -> monthly hosted cost saving ~ $67.5k (gross) per cohort aggregate; subtract KV cost -> strong ROI.
- Mid cohort at 10k slots -> P=0.21 -> token reduction ~4.3M tokens -> $6.45k saved; payback in ~5 months across cohort share.

Scenario B (dedicated customers): reserved marginal token cost $0.0008. If Redwood includes KV as part of Dedicated SKU (no charge), per-token value from cache is lower, but retention of customers and lower churn must be considered. For Top cohort, switching from hosted to dedicated reduces per-token savings number but still justifies storage cost at >5k slots.

SENSITIVITY TABLE (text):
Variable | Low | Base | High | Impact on payback (direction)
Token price (per-token blended) | $0.0009 | $0.0015 | $0.0022 | higher price -> faster payback (positive)
Avg tokens/req (Top cohort) | 420 | 520 | 680 | higher tokens -> bigger savings
KV monthly cost per 10k slots | $6 | $12 | $22 | higher cost -> slower payback (negative)
Hit-curve asymptote (Top cohort A) | 0.6 | 0.72 | 0.84 | higher A -> faster payback

EXAMPLE PAYBACK CALC (Top cohort, base numbers):
- Estimated monthly token reduction per top-client average: 4.5M tokens
- Hosted $ saving/month/client = 4.5M * $0.0015 = $6,750
- If we charge $30/month for 10k slots and allocate 10k slots -> provider margin per client = $6,720 (net)
- Payback on any one-time provisioning/setup cost (e.g., $1,200) = <1 month. (Note: numbers aggregated across top cohort population show substantial runway for offering an enterprise add-on).

RECOMMENDATIONS (draft):
- Pilot: Offer a "KV reserved tier" as a paid add-on only to Top cohort clients (automatic eligibility detection via usage telemetry). Start with a 3-month opt-in for a subset (n=25 clients) to validate hit-curve in production and reconcile modeled vs observed hit-rate.
- Pricing: start with $30/month per 10k slots, include a usage-based rebate if actual hit-rate < modeled threshold at month end to reduce adoption friction.
- Product: expose per-client hit-curve preview in Console (visualize estimated projected savings for their current traffic) so sales can present ROI to customers.
- Engineering: instrument a lightweight sample-grade tracer to validate per-prefix TTL and entropy assumptions; add an endpoint to export anonymized sample traces for model tuning.

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS (working list):
- Does per-client prefix privacy or PII policy constrain caching semantics? Need security review (contact: security@redwood.ai).
- Operational cost variance: S3 request costs for very high churn prefixes might be underestimated in amortized storage cost. Add S3 request simulation in next iteration.
- Churn effect: if top clients reduce usage after seeing cost separation, model will overestimate long-term ROI. Include retention experiments in pilot.

NEXT STEPS / ACTION ITEMS:
- PM (Priya): schedule pilot cohort outreach and define acceptance criteria (hit-rate delta threshold, conversion to paid tier).
- Eng (Elliot + Diego): implement sample tracer and quick simulation harness to run live-vs-sim comparisons; due 2026-02-05.
- Data (Sara): run anonymized cohort extraction and provide 90/50/10 percentile telemetry snapshots; due 2025-12-08.

NOTES TO SELF (informal):
- The logistic hit-curve is a convenient analytic approximation but real client traces show multi-modal reuse patterns; follow-up should test mixture models.
- Consider bundling cache tiers as part of Dedicated SKUs rather than standalone in markets where sales friction is high.

APPENDIX (quick formulas):
- Monthly_kv_cost = (slots / 10000) * KV_unit_price_per_10k
- Token_savings = total_tokens * hit_rate_estimated * (avg_output_frac)
- Dollars_saved = Token_savings * token_price

End of working draft.

(If copying into a proper spreadsheet, columns are: cohort, clients_count, tokens_month, slots_allocated, hit_rate_est, token_savings, dollar_savings, kv_cost, net_saving, payback_months)
